messages:
sasha (ml-eng): New customer request to onboard Equinox-100B for Redwood Private (VPC). Customer needs low-latency inference (p95 < 120ms for 512 tokens) and an int8 quant path. They can provide an eval set and are willing to pay for dedicated capacity. Link: https://huggingface.co/equinox/equinox-100b

sasha (ml-eng): Sample start command they shared: 
```bash
run_infer --model-path ./equinox-100b --dtype float16 --max-seq 512
```

deepak (infra-ml): looping in. Quick Qs: which tokenizer/version? any custom ops/weights layout? perf target per-GPU or multi-GPU?

sasha (ml-eng): tokenizer = eqx-tokenizer v1, no custom ops per vendor note. Config gist: https://gist.github.com/equinox/conf-12345. Perf target is single-stream (batch=1) p95 <= 120ms on A100-80GB (dedicated).

quant-bot: Automated triage: model ~96B params (est), FLOPs ~1.8e12. Int8 path (AWQ/L2) likely reduces memory ~2.5x; expect ~10-20% risk of quality delta on some prompts. Recommended next steps: 1) smoke-run FP16 on Dedicated test pool 2) collect 500 representative prompts + refs from customer 3) run AWQ int8 baseline + golden eval. Tagging: triage/needs-smoke.

linda (customer-eng): Customer confirms they will upload eval set and requires VPC + KMS. Also requests SLA in contract (uptime + latency).

mike (oncall): I can schedule a smoke-run tomorrow 09:00 PT. How many GPUs should I allocate? 1 A100 should be enough for FP16 smoke, but we'll need 2+ for throughput tests. deepak — want to own quant baselines?

deepak (infra-ml): I can own quant baseline. Plan: FP16 smoke -> AWQ int8 -> compare metrics. Will start with 1 A100 single-stream FP16, then AWQ offline. ETA 48 hours for initial baselines.

sasha (ml-eng): Great. I'll coordinate with customer for eval dataset + access. Quick checklist I'm adding here: 
- [ ] allocate dedicated test pool (1x A100)
- [ ] run FP16 smoke (latency + mem)
- [ ] collect 500 prompts + refs from customer
- [ ] run AWQ int8 baseline + eval
- [ ] compare p95 / quality-regression / cost delta
- [ ] decision: onboard (dedicated) vs. require further optimization

mike (oncall): :thumbsup:
